2026-11-01.title: First Sunday of the Dedication of the Church (Qudash Edtha)
2026-11-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Comfort for the people: those who wait for the Lord
Christ entered the tent not made with hands
Those who were ready went in to the wedding feast
2026-11-01.alt: The season of the Dedication of the Church (Qudash Edtha), the last four weeks of the liturgical year, begins. In the Latin Church today is the Solemnity of All Saints; in the Syro-Malabar Church All Saints is kept on the Friday after Easter.
2026-11-01.verse: Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
theo: The Syro-Malabar year ends as it began: looking at the Church. For four weeks, Qudash Edtha, the Dedication of the Church, invites us to contemplate the Church as the Bride whom Christ will present to the Father, and as God's dwelling among his people. The readings follow that dwelling from the desert to the end of time.

In the desert Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp. Whoever seeks the Lord goes out to it; the pillar of cloud comes down to its door, and “the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.” God wants friendship with his people, and he chooses a place to meet them.

The Letter to the Hebrews tells us what that tent was pointing to. Christ, the high priest, has entered “the greater and perfect tent, not made with hands”, not with the blood of animals but with his own blood. The Church on earth is the doorway to that sanctuary: every Qurbana is our entry, with Christ, into the Holy of Holies.

The Gospel adds the note of the season: readiness. Ten virgins wait for the bridegroom; five have oil, five do not. The door opens for those who are ready, and then it is shut. The Church is the Bride waiting for the Bridegroom. Oil cannot be borrowed at the last minute: it is faith, prayer and love stored up day by day. Isaiah promises that those who wait for the Lord will not grow weary. The waiting itself becomes strength.
conn: Outside the camp.

Moses pitched the tent “outside the camp” (Exodus 33:7). Hebrews 13:12–13 says Jesus suffered “outside the city gate” and invites us to go to him “outside the camp”. The meeting place with God is where Christ is, even when that place is costly.
The Temple not made with hands.
Jesus spoke of “this temple made with hands” and another “not made with hands” (Mark 14:58), meaning his body (John 2:21). Hebrews 9:11 uses the same expression: the true sanctuary is Christ himself.
Eagles' wings.
Isaiah 40:31 echoes Exodus 19:4: “I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.” The God who carried Israel out of Egypt carries the weary today.
Ten virgins, ten lamps.

At Jewish weddings the bridegroom came at night to take his bride home, and the guests went out with torches to meet him. Jesus is the Bridegroom (Mark 2:19); the Church is the Bride (Revelation 19:7).
altar: Hebrews describes the high priest entering the sanctuary once a year with blood. At the Qurbana the veil is opened and the priest goes up to the madbaha: we are shown that Christ has opened the way into the sanctuary for all. In the Holy Mysteries the Bridegroom comes to his Bride already now; each Communion is oil for our lamps.
outline: Opening
Ask: if Christ came tonight, would your lamp be burning? The Church ends her year with that question.
Point 1 · The tent of meeting
God speaks to Moses face to face, as to a friend. The Church is our tent of meeting; prayer is our friendship.
Point 2 · The tent not made with hands
Christ has entered the true sanctuary with his own blood. Every Qurbana takes us there with him.
Point 3 · Oil that cannot be borrowed
Faith and love cannot be borrowed at the last minute. Store oil daily: prayer, sacraments, works of mercy.
Closing image
A small oil lamp (nilavilakku) kept burning in a Kerala home at dusk: faithful, quiet, every day.
Take-home line
“My lamp will be burning when the Bridegroom comes.”
live: Visit the tent of meeting (Exodus 33:7)
Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, speaking to the Lord as to a friend.
Store oil (Matthew 25:4)
Choose one daily habit of prayer for these four weeks and keep it faithfully.
Wait without wearying (Isaiah 40:31)
Name one burden that wears you out and offer it to the Lord each morning.
fathers: St Augustine
Commenting on the virgins, he says the oil is love, which shines in good works; it cannot be bought from others when the Bridegroom is at the door (Sermon 93).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He sings of the Church as the Bride whom the Bridegroom betrothed with his blood and adorned with his Mysteries (Hymns on the Church).
magis: Lumen Gentium 6
The Church is called the tabernacle of God among men, the holy temple, the spotless spouse of the spotless Lamb.
Catechism 1036, 1056
Watchfulness and the call to conversion in view of Christ's coming.
saints: 2 November: Commemoration of the Dead (All Souls). 5 November: Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth.
2026-11-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, you have entered the true sanctuary with your own blood. Keep our lamps burning with faith and love, that when you come we may be ready and enter with you into the wedding feast. Amen.

2026-11-08.title: Second Sunday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: I will bring you into the promised land
My reward is with the Lord
An inheritance kept in heaven for you
You will sit on twelve thrones
2026-11-08.alt: Season of the Dedication of the Church (Qudash Edtha).
2026-11-08.verse: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life.
theo: Today's readings speak of inheritance. In Egypt, crushed by slavery, Israel hears God's promise: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God… I will bring you into the land… I will give it to you for a possession.” The promised land was never only a territory; it was life with God.

The Servant in Isaiah feels he has laboured in vain, “yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.” Peter writes to scattered Christians that they have been born anew “into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.” The Church is the people already on the way to that inheritance.

In the Gospel the disciples are shocked: if the rich can hardly enter the Kingdom, who can be saved? Jesus answers, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.” Then Peter asks what they will receive for leaving everything. Jesus promises thrones, a hundredfold, and eternal life. The apostles, on whom the Church is founded, will share in Christ's judgement and glory.

For Kerala Christians, whose families have often been measured by land and property, this Gospel is searching. Our deepest inheritance is not the family property but the faith received from the apostle Thomas and handed down for centuries. What we leave for Christ is never lost; it returns a hundredfold.
conn: Four “I will” promises.

Exodus 6:6–8 has a chain of divine promises: I will free, deliver, redeem, take you as my people. Jewish tradition links them to the four cups of the Passover meal; at the Last Supper Jesus took one of those cups and made it the cup of the new covenant.
Light to the nations.
Isaiah 49:6 calls the Servant “a light to the nations”. Simeon applies this to the child Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2:32), and Paul to the Church's mission (Acts 13:47).
Twelve thrones.
The twelve apostles correspond to the twelve tribes: the Church is the renewed Israel. Revelation 21:14 places the apostles' names on the twelve foundations of the heavenly Jerusalem.
The eye of a needle.
Some later explanations speak of a small gate called the “needle's eye”, but there is no ancient evidence for it. Jesus deliberately uses an impossible image: salvation is God's work.
altar: Peter calls our inheritance “kept in heaven”. At the Qurbana we receive its pledge already: the Body and Blood of the risen Christ, “the medicine of immortality”, as St Ignatius of Antioch called it. Every Communion is a down payment on the inheritance.
outline: Opening
Ask: what will you leave behind for your children? Land, house, money, or faith?
Point 1 · God's promise of an inheritance
From Egypt to the promised land: God frees his people to belong to him.
Point 2 · An inheritance that does not fade
Peter: a living hope and a heavenly inheritance, tested like gold in fire.
Point 3 · Impossible for us, possible for God
Wealth cannot save; God's grace can. What we leave for Christ returns a hundredfold.
Closing image
An old Kerala family Bible handed down for generations: the true family property.
Take-home line
“My inheritance is the Lord.”
live: Hand on the faith (1 Peter 1:4)
Talk with your children this week about how faith came to your family.
Loosen one attachment (Matthew 19:24)
Give something valuable to someone in need, freely.
Trust God with the impossible (Matthew 19:26)
Bring one “impossible” situation to God each day.
fathers: St Clement of Alexandria
In “Who is the rich man that shall be saved?” he teaches that wealth itself is not condemned, but the soul's attachment to it; riches must be used for others.
St Ignatius of Antioch
He calls the Eucharist “the medicine of immortality, the antidote against death” (Letter to the Ephesians 20).
magis: Catechism 2544–2547
Detachment from riches is necessary to enter the Kingdom.
Catechism 1817–1821
Hope: we desire eternal life as our happiness, trusting in Christ's promises.
saints: 11 Nov: St Martin of Tours (Latin calendar). 12 Nov: St Josaphat, martyr for unity (Latin calendar).
2026-11-08.prayer: Father of mercy, you have given us new birth into a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven. Free us from all that holds us back from following your Son, and make us faithful to the faith we have received, for all things are possible with you. Amen.

2026-11-15.title: Third Sunday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Jacob works seven years for Rachel
2026-11-15.alt: Season of the Dedication of the Church (Qudash Edtha).
2026-11-15.verse: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and trustworthy slave; you have been trustworthy in a few things, I will put you in charge of many things; enter into the joy of your master.’
theo: As the liturgical year draws to its close, the Church looks at work: our daily labour and the work of the Kingdom. Jacob works seven years for Rachel, “and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.” Love transforms labour. Sirach adds: “Stand by your agreement… grow old in your work… trust in the Lord and keep at your job.”

Paul is blunt with Christians in Thessalonica who stopped working because they thought the Lord's return was imminent: “Anyone unwilling to work should not eat.” Waiting for Christ is never an excuse for idleness; it is the reason for faithful work.

In the parable of the talents, a master entrusts his property to three servants “each according to his ability”. Two trade and double what they received; the third buries his talent out of fear. The master praises the faithful ones: “Well done, good and trustworthy slave… enter into the joy of your master.” The talents are all God's gifts: life, faith, abilities, time, the sacraments. What matters is not how much we have received but whether we have used it for him.

The Church, the Bride, is not a museum guarding a buried treasure; she is a household where every member is given something to invest. On the last Sundays of the year the Lord asks each of us: what have you done with what I gave you?
conn: Seven years like a few days.

Jacob's love for Rachel (Genesis 29:20) is echoed in Song of Songs 8:7: “Many waters cannot quench love.” Love makes long service light, as Jesus says: “My yoke is easy, and my burden is light” (Matthew 11:30).
A talent was huge.

A talent was about 6,000 denarii, roughly twenty years' wages for a labourer. Even the “one talent” servant received a fortune. The parable gave the English word “talent” its meaning of a natural gift.
Paul the tentmaker.
Paul worked with his own hands making tents (Acts 18:3; 20:34) so as not to burden anyone. He preached work by doing it.
The joy of the master.
“Enter into the joy of your master” anticipates the wedding feast (Matthew 25:10) and the Kingdom prepared for the blessed (Matthew 25:34). Faithful work ends in joy.
altar: At the offertory bread and wine are brought to the altar, “fruit of the earth and work of human hands”. Our work is taken up into Christ's sacrifice. The Qurbana is where our talents are offered back to God and returned to us transformed, as the Body of Christ.
outline: Opening
Ask: what gift has God given you that you have buried?
Point 1 · Love makes labour light
Jacob's seven years seemed a few days. Work done for love is never wasted.
Point 2 · Waiting is not idleness
Paul: work quietly and earn your living. The Christian waits for Christ by working faithfully.
Point 3 · Invest what you have received
The talents are God's gifts. Fear buries them; faith invests them.
Closing image
A farmer in Kuttanad planting rice: he trusts the harvest and works the field.
Take-home line
“I will use what God gave me, for him.”
live: Unbury one talent (Matthew 25:25)
Offer one skill (music, teaching, accounts, cooking) to your parish this month.
Work for love (Genesis 29:20)
Offer your work tomorrow morning to God for someone you love.
Honest labour (2 Thessalonians 3:12)
Do a full day's honest work without cutting corners.
fathers: St Gregory the Great
“Whoever has understanding should take care not to be silent; whoever has wealth should not grow sluggish in mercy… for the talent received will be demanded” (Homilies on the Gospels 9).
St John Chrysostom
He notes that the master gives each “according to his ability”: God asks of us not what we do not have, but what we have.
magis: Laborem Exercens 25–27
St John Paul II: through work the human person shares in the work of the Creator and in the Cross of Christ.
Catechism 2427–2428
Human work proceeds from persons created in God's image; it can be a means of sanctification.
saints: 21 November: Entrance of St Thomas the Apostle into India; Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-11-15.prayer: Lord God, you have entrusted us with many gifts. Free us from the fear that buries them, give us faithful hearts to use them for your Kingdom, and let us hear at the end: “Well done, good and trustworthy servant; enter into the joy of your master.” Amen.

2026-11-22.title: Fourth Sunday of the Dedication of the Church · Feast of Christ the King
2026-11-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Melchizedek, priest of God Most High
Israel rejects the Lord as King
King of kings and Lord of lords
2026-11-22.alt: Last Sunday of the liturgical year. Next Sunday (29 November) the new liturgical year begins with the First Sunday of Annunciation (Suvara), First Set.
2026-11-22.verse: Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.”
theo: The liturgical year ends with a crown. On the last Sunday of Qudash Edtha the Church proclaims Christ the King. Pope Pius XI instituted the feast in 1925 (Quas Primas) for a world that was trying to organise itself without God; the question is no less urgent today.

The readings show two kinds of kingship. Melchizedek, “king of Salem” (peace) and “priest of God Most High”, brings out bread and wine and blesses Abraham: a mysterious figure of Christ, King and Priest, who offers bread and wine. Centuries later Israel demands “a king like other nations”, and God tells Samuel: “they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from being king over them.” Every time we choose earthly powers over God, we repeat Israel's demand.

Before Pilate, bound and condemned, Jesus says: “My kingdom is not from this world.” His kingship does not come from armies, money or votes; it comes from the truth. “For this I was born… to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.” His throne is the Cross; his crown is of thorns.

Revelation shows the end: heaven opened, a rider called Faithful and True, his robe dipped in blood, his name “The Word of God”, and on his robe: “King of kings and Lord of lords.” The Church, the Bride, ends her year by bowing before her King and Bridegroom. The question for each of us: does Christ reign in my home, my work, my phone, my choices?
conn: Bread and wine.

Melchizedek's bread and wine (Genesis 14:18) and Psalm 110:4, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek,” are applied to Christ in Hebrews 7. The Fathers saw in this offering a figure of the Eucharist.
“A king like other nations.”
Israel's demand (1 Samuel 8:5) echoes in the crowd's cry before Pilate: “We have no king but the emperor” (John 19:15). Both reject God's kingship.
The Son of Man's kingdom.
Daniel 7:13–14 sees “one like a son of man” receiving an everlasting kingdom. Jesus applies this to himself before the high priest (Mark 14:62).
The inscription.
Pilate wrote “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews” in Hebrew, Latin and Greek (John 19:19–20): the first public proclamation of Christ's kingship, in the languages of the world.
altar: Melchizedek, king and priest, offered bread and wine; Christ, our King and High Priest, offers himself under the signs of bread and wine. At the Qurbana the King comes not to be served but to serve, and to give his life. To receive him is to accept his reign in us.
outline: Opening
Ask: who really rules your life? Look at your calendar, your bank statement and your phone's screen time.
Point 1 · King and Priest
Melchizedek's bread and wine point to Christ, King of peace and eternal Priest.
Point 2 · “We want a king like the nations”
Israel rejected God as King. We do the same when money, power or opinion rule us.
Point 3 · A kingdom not of this world
Christ reigns from the Cross, by truth and love. Whoever belongs to the truth listens to his voice.
Closing image
The rider of Revelation: King of kings and Lord of lords. The year ends at his feet.
Take-home line
“Jesus, reign in me.”
live: Enthrone Christ at home (Revelation 19:16)
Place a picture or crucifix of Christ the King prominently and consecrate your family to him.
Listen to his voice (John 18:37)
Choose truth in one situation where a lie would be easier.
Reject other kings (1 Samuel 8:7)
Name one thing that rules you instead of God, and dethrone it this week.
fathers: St Augustine
On John 18: “Hear, Jews and Gentiles… I do not hinder your rule in this world. My kingdom is not of this world. Come and believe; do not be afraid” (Tractates on John 115).
St Cyprian of Carthage
He sees Melchizedek's offering of bread and wine as a figure of the Lord's sacrifice (Letter 63).
magis: Pius XI, Quas Primas (1925)
Christ reigns in minds, wills and hearts; peace is possible only in the Kingdom of Christ.
Catechism 2105
The duty of offering God genuine worship concerns man both individually and socially; the Church announces Christ's kingship over all creation.
saints: 24 November: Vietnamese martyrs (Latin calendar). 28 November (celebrated for 29 November): St Andrew the Apostle.
2026-11-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, King of kings and Lord of lords, Priest forever in the order of Melchizedek, reign in our hearts, our families and our society. Make us belong to the truth and listen to your voice, until we see you in your glory. Amen.

2026-11-29.title: First Sunday of Annunciation (Suvara) · New Liturgical Year
2026-11-29.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Announcement of the birth of Isaac
Announcement of the birth of John the Baptist
2026-11-29.alt: The new liturgical year begins with the season of Annunciation–Nativity (Suvara–Yalda). In the Holy Qurbana the second Anaphora (Qudasha of Mar Theodore) is used from today until Palm Sunday. The 25 Days' Fast before Christmas begins (traditionally from 1 December; check your eparchy).
2026-11-29.verse: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
theo: A new liturgical year begins, and the Syro-Malabar Church begins it not with the end of the world but with an announcement: good news is coming. The season of Suvara (Annunciation) leads us through the great announcements of salvation, to Zechariah, to Mary, to Joseph, until the Nativity of the Lord.

The first announcement is made to old people who had given up hope. Abraham is ninety-nine and Sarah ninety; Abraham falls on his face and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” Centuries later Zechariah and Elizabeth are “righteous before God”, yet childless and “getting on in years”. In both stories God does the impossible and gives a son through whom the whole plan of salvation moves forward.

Zechariah is a priest serving in the Temple. As he offers incense, the angel Gabriel says: “Do not be afraid… your prayer has been heard.” Perhaps Zechariah had long stopped praying for a child; God had not stopped listening. His son John will go before the Lord “to turn the hearts of parents to their children… to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.” The preparation for Christ begins in a family.

That is why the Epistle speaks of the family: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Husbands, wives, children and parents are the first place where salvation is lived. Isaiah's words are spoken over each family at the start of this year: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.”
conn: Two births announced.

The births of Isaac and John follow the same pattern: an aged, barren couple, a divine promise, human doubt (Abraham laughs, Zechariah questions), and the gift of a son. Luke deliberately echoes Genesis to show that the God of Abraham is acting again.
The spirit of Elijah.

Gabriel's words about John (Luke 1:17) quote Malachi 4:5–6, the last words of the Old Testament prophets: Elijah will come and turn the hearts of parents to their children. The Gospel begins where the Old Testament ended.
The hour of incense.
Zechariah receives the announcement at the hour of incense, when the people pray outside (Luke 1:10). Psalm 141:2: “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you.” The Gospel begins in the liturgy.
Gabriel.

The angel who appears to Zechariah is the same who explained the seventy weeks to Daniel “at the time of the evening sacrifice” (Daniel 9:21). Gabriel's coming signals that the long-awaited time is fulfilled.
altar: The Gospel opens in the sanctuary, with a priest at the altar of incense. In our Qurbana, too, incense rises and the priest prays for the people. From today we use the Anaphora of Mar Theodore, one of the three ancient anaphoras of the East Syriac tradition. As Zechariah received the good news at the altar, so do we: the Word who was announced comes to us in the Mysteries.
outline: Opening
Ask: what prayer have you stopped praying because you lost hope?
Point 1 · God of the impossible
Abraham laughs, Zechariah doubts, God keeps his promise. Nothing is impossible for him.
Point 2 · Your prayer has been heard
God hears even prayers we have forgotten. The Annunciation season is a season of renewed hope.
Point 3 · The family prepares the way
John will turn the hearts of parents to children. Christ comes through families: make your home a place of preparation.
Closing image
An elderly couple in a Kerala parish lighting the first candle of the season together.
Take-home line
“Do not be afraid; your prayer has been heard.”
live: Renew a lost prayer (Luke 1:13)
Take up again one intention you stopped praying for, and pray it daily until Christmas.
Keep the 25 Days' Fast
Decide as a family how you will fast and pray during these weeks.
Honour one another (Ephesians 5:21)
Do one act of service for each member of your family this week.
fathers: St Ambrose
On Zechariah's silence: he was punished not for asking but for not believing; yet the punishment was mercy, for his silence ended in the Benedictus (Commentary on Luke 1).
St Ephrem the Syrian
In his Hymns on the Nativity he sings that the barren gave birth so that the Virgin's child-bearing would be believed: Elizabeth's son prepared for Mary's Son.
magis: Amoris Laetitia 86–88
The family is the place where faith is first handed on; the Church is a family of families.
Catechism 524
The Church celebrates the waiting for the Messiah each year, sharing in the long preparation for the Saviour's first coming.
saints: 3 December: St Francis Xavier, apostle of India. First Friday: 4 December.
2026-11-29.prayer: Lord God, faithful to your promises, at the beginning of this new year you speak to us as to Zechariah: “Do not be afraid; your prayer has been heard.” Renew our hope, bless our families, and prepare our hearts to welcome your Son. Amen.

2026-11-02.title: First Monday of the Dedication of the Church · Commemoration of the Dead
2026-11-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The Lord will make you live
Hope in the resurrection of the dead
We will not all die, but we will all be changed
Jesus is the resurrection and the life
2026-11-02.alt: Readings of the weekday: 2 Corinthians 4:13–18 (Momentary affliction prepares an eternal weight of glory); John 16:16–24 (Your joy will be complete).
2026-11-02.verse: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live.
theo: Today the whole Church prays for the faithful departed. We do it not out of sentiment alone but out of faith: we believe in the resurrection of the body, and we believe in the communion of saints, in which the living and the dead remain one family in Christ.

Ezekiel stands in a valley of dry bones. “Can these bones live?” God answers by his word and his Spirit: “I will open your graves… I will put my spirit within you, and you shall live.” What seemed final is not final for God. Judas Maccabeus, finding that fallen soldiers had worn idols, prays and offers a sacrifice for them, “so that they might be delivered from their sin”. Scripture calls it “a holy and pious thought”. Here the Church finds an ancient witness to prayer for the dead.

The Catholic faith teaches that those who die in God's grace but are not yet fully purified undergo a purification after death, which the Church calls purgatory, so as to enter the joy of heaven (Catechism 1030–1032). Our prayers, and above all the Holy Qurbana offered for them, help them. This is love that death does not end.

At Bethany, Martha meets Jesus with grief and faith: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” Jesus answers not with an explanation but with himself: “I am the resurrection and the life.” Christian hope is not an idea about the afterlife; it is a Person who has conquered death. With Paul we can say: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
conn: Breath and Spirit.

In Ezekiel 37 the same Hebrew word, ruach, means breath, wind and spirit. As God breathed into Adam (Genesis 2:7), he breathes again into the dead. On Easter night the risen Jesus “breathed on them and said, ‘Receive the Holy Spirit’” (John 20:22).
Martha's confession.

Martha's words, “You are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world” (John 11:27), match Peter's confession in Matthew 16:16. A grieving woman makes one of the great professions of faith in the Gospels.
The last trumpet.
Paul's “last trumpet” (1 Corinthians 15:52) recalls the trumpet at Sinai (Exodus 19:16) and the trumpet of the Day of the Lord (Joel 2:1): God's final coming to his people.
altar: From the earliest centuries Christians have offered the Eucharist for the dead. In every Qurbana the Church remembers the departed in the anaphora. Have the Qurbana offered for your dead: it is the greatest gift we can give them, for it is Christ's own sacrifice, which has conquered death.
outline: Opening
Ask: whom do you miss today? Name them silently before God.
Point 1 · Can these bones live?
Ezekiel's valley: God's word and Spirit bring life where there is none.
Point 2 · A holy and pious thought
Judas Maccabeus prays for the dead. The Church prays for the souls being purified, out of love.
Point 3 · I am the resurrection
Jesus answers grief with himself. Our hope is a Person.
Closing image
A Kerala family at the cemetery with candles and flowers: grief held in faith.
Take-home line
“Love does not end at the grave; it becomes prayer.”
live: Pray for your dead by name (2 Maccabees 12:45)
Write the names of your departed family members and pray for them each evening this month.
Have a Qurbana offered
Request a Qurbana for the souls in purgatory, especially the forgotten.
Visit the cemetery (John 11:17)
Visit a grave this week, clean it, and pray there with your family.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
“Let us help and commemorate them… Why would you doubt that our offerings for the dead bring them some consolation?” (Homily on 1 Corinthians 41).
St Ephrem the Syrian
In his testament he asked his brothers to remember him in their prayers and offerings after his death.
magis: Catechism 1030–1032
Purgatory; the Church's prayer and Eucharistic sacrifice for the dead.
Catechism 958
Communion with the dead: our prayer for them can help them and make their intercession for us effective.
saints: The whole month is traditionally dedicated to praying for the faithful departed.
2026-11-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, grant to our departed brothers and sisters eternal rest. Purify them in your mercy, bring them into the light of your face, and keep us in the hope of meeting them again in your Kingdom. Amen.

2026-11-03.title: First Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: We long for our heavenly dwelling
The son returns to his father's house
2026-11-03.verse: But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
theo: Paul speaks of our body as a tent that will be folded up, and of “a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” In this season of the Church we remember that our true home is the Father's house.

The younger son learns this the hard way. Far from home, hungry among pigs, he “came to himself” and set out for his father's house. The father was already watching the road. Every confession is this homecoming: the Church is the house where the Father runs to meet us.
outline: Opening
Ask: what does “home” mean to you?
Point 1 · A tent and a house
Our earthly life is a tent; God prepares an eternal home (2 Corinthians 5:1).
Point 2 · He came to himself
Conversion begins when we remember the Father's house.
Point 3 · The father ran
God runs to meet the returning sinner; confession is homecoming.
Take-home line
“The Father is watching the road for me.”
live: Go home (Luke 15:18)
Plan a good confession this month.
Long for heaven (2 Corinthians 5:2)
Pray each evening: “Lord, bring me home to you.”
2026-11-03.prayer: Merciful Father, you watch the road for every child who is far away. Bring me home to your house, forgive me, and clothe me again with your love. Amen.

2026-11-04.title: First Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The chief Shepherd will give the crown of glory
2026-11-04.verse: Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?… Feed my lambs.
theo: The Church is a flock with a Shepherd. Peter, who once denied the Lord, is asked three times, “Do you love me?” and three times receives the charge: “Feed my lambs… tend my sheep.” Authority in the Church is born of love and exists for service.

Years later Peter writes to the elders: “Tend the flock of God that is in your charge… not for sordid gain but eagerly… be examples to the flock.” He had learned shepherding from the Shepherd. Today pray for your bishop and parish priest, and ask how you too shepherd those entrusted to you.
outline: Opening
Ask: who has shepherded you in faith?
Point 1 · Do you love me?
Love is the first qualification for every ministry.
Point 2 · Feed my sheep
Pastors serve the flock that belongs to Christ.
Point 3 · Examples to the flock
Parents, catechists and teachers shepherd by example.
Take-home line
“Love first, then serve.”
live: Pray for your shepherds (1 Peter 5:2)
Pray by name for your bishop and parish priest today.
Shepherd at home (John 21:15)
Spend time with a child or younger person and speak to them of faith.
2026-11-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, give your Church shepherds after your own heart. Teach me to love you first and to serve those you entrust to me. Amen.

2026-11-05.title: First Thursday of the Dedication of the Church · Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth
2026-11-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The Gentiles are fellow heirs of the promise
The healing of the centurion's servant
2026-11-05.alt: For Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth: Colossians 1:21–23 (Continue in the faith, stable and steadfast); Luke 1:5–25 (The Lord's mercy on Zechariah and Elizabeth).
2026-11-05.verse: Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only speak the word, and my servant will be healed.
theo: A Roman centurion, a Gentile and an officer of the occupying army, comes to Jesus for his servant. His humility and faith astonish Jesus: “In no one in Israel have I found such faith.” Then Jesus opens the horizon: “Many will come from east and west and will eat with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.”

Paul calls this the mystery hidden for ages and now revealed: the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body. We Indians are among those who came “from the east”. The centurion's words have become the prayer of the Church before Communion: Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word.
outline: Opening
Ask: when do you say “Lord, I am not worthy”? Do you mean it?
Point 1 · Faith that astonishes Jesus
A Gentile soldier teaches Israel what faith is.
Point 2 · From east and west
The Church gathers all nations, including us.
Point 3 · Only say the word
Humility and trust before Communion.
Take-home line
“Only say the word.”
live: Pray with the centurion (Matthew 8:8)
Before Communion, say his words slowly and mean them.
Pray for a sick person (Matthew 8:6)
Intercede for one sick person you know, as the centurion did.
saints: Parents of John the Baptist, “righteous before God” (Luke 1:6), who waited long and kept praying.
2026-11-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. Gather all nations into your Kingdom. Amen.

2026-11-06.title: First Friday of the Dedication of the Church · First Friday
2026-11-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Reward for those who repent and believe
2026-11-06.alt: First Friday: devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
2026-11-06.verse: For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him.
theo: A father asks his two sons to work in the vineyard. One refuses and later repents and goes; the other promises and does not go. Jesus asks which did the father's will. Words are not enough; conversion shows itself in deeds.

Paul applies this to everyday relationships: children and parents, workers and employers. Do your work “as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” On this First Friday we look at the Heart of Jesus, who did the Father's will to the end, and ask for a heart that obeys in deeds.
outline: Opening
Ask: how many promises to God have I made and not kept?
Point 1 · Two sons
Repentance that acts is better than promises that do not.
Point 2 · Work as service to Christ
Ordinary work done from the heart is worship.
Point 3 · The Sacred Heart
Jesus' heart obeyed the Father to the end; ask for such a heart.
Take-home line
“Not only yes in words, but yes in deeds.”
live: Keep one promise (Matthew 21:30)
Do today one thing you promised God and postponed.
Work for Christ (Ephesians 6:7)
Offer your day's work to the Sacred Heart this morning.
2026-11-06.prayer: Sacred Heart of Jesus, you did the Father's will with love to the end. Give me a heart that obeys not only in words but in deeds, and make my daily work an offering to you. Amen.

2026-11-07.title: First Saturday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Love is the way to eternal life: the Good Samaritan
2026-11-07.verse: He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
theo: A lawyer asks, “What must I do to inherit eternal life?” and then, “Who is my neighbour?” Jesus answers with a story in which the despised Samaritan is the one who stops, binds the wounds and pays the cost. The question changes: not “Who is my neighbour?” but “Will I be a neighbour?”

Paul describes the same love from the inside: “Let love be genuine… outdo one another in showing honour… extend hospitality to strangers… live peaceably with all.” The Church, God's house, is meant to be the inn where the wounded are cared for, and every Christian is sent out to the road to Jericho.
outline: Opening
Ask: who lies wounded on your road this week?
Point 1 · The question behind the question
“Who is my neighbour?” becomes “Will I be a neighbour?”
Point 2 · Love that stops
The Samaritan's love costs time, oil and money.
Point 3 · The Church as the inn
The Church is where the wounded are brought and cared for.
Take-home line
“Go and do likewise.”
live: Stop for someone (Luke 10:33)
Give time today to someone others pass by.
Show hospitality (Romans 12:13)
Welcome a stranger, newcomer or migrant worker this week.
2026-11-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Samaritan of humanity, you stopped for me when I was wounded. Make me a neighbour to all, with genuine love that stops, binds and pays the cost. Amen.

2026-11-09.title: Second Monday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Christ is the head of the Church
2026-11-09.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: Paul's great hymn proclaims Christ as the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation, “the head of the body, the church”. Everything was created through him and for him, and in him all things hold together.

At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God,” and Jesus builds his Church on that rock. The Church has Christ as head and Peter as the visible foundation of unity. Our Syro-Malabar Church lives this: an ancient apostolic tradition in full communion with the successor of Peter.
outline: Opening
Ask: who is Jesus for you, in one sentence?
Point 1 · Christ the head
In him all things hold together (Colossians 1:17).
Point 2 · Peter's confession
Faith revealed by the Father, not by flesh and blood.
Point 3 · The rock
The Church is built on Peter; the gates of Hades will not prevail.
Take-home line
“You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
live: Confess Christ (Matthew 16:16)
Pray Peter's confession slowly this morning and evening.
Pray for unity (Matthew 16:18)
Pray for the Pope and for our Major Archbishop today.
2026-11-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, head of the Church, you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. Build us on the rock of Peter's faith and keep your Church one. Amen.

2026-11-10.title: Second Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
2026-11-10.verse: Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
theo: Peter, near the end of his life, remembers the mountain: “we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty… We ourselves heard this voice come from heaven.” The faith of the Church rests on eyewitnesses and on the prophetic word, “a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns.”

On the mountain Jesus prays and is transfigured; Moses and Elijah speak with him of his departure in Jerusalem. The glory prepares the disciples for the Cross. The Church, in her last season, looks toward the same glory: the day when the Morning Star rises in our hearts.
outline: Opening
Ask: when have you glimpsed God's glory?
Point 1 · Eyewitnesses
Our faith rests on apostolic witness, not clever myths.
Point 2 · Listen to him
The Father points to the Son.
Point 3 · Glory before the Cross
The Transfiguration strengthens us for suffering.
Take-home line
“This is my Son: listen to him.”
live: Listen to him (Luke 9:35)
Read today's Gospel slowly and keep one phrase.
Pray as Jesus did (Luke 9:29)
Give ten minutes to silent prayer today.
2026-11-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, transfigured in glory, let me listen to you and be changed by your light, until the day dawns and the Morning Star rises in my heart. Amen.

2026-11-11.title: Second Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb
2026-11-11.verse: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
theo: Heaven bursts into song: “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns… the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.” The whole history of salvation is a love story that ends in a wedding: Christ and his Church.

In Jesus' parable the invited guests make excuses, and the king fills the hall with people from the streets, “both good and bad”. But one guest has no wedding garment. The invitation is free, but it must be received: the garment is the new life of grace put on in baptism and kept clean by conversion.
outline: Opening
Ask: what excuses do we give God?
Point 1 · The wedding of the Lamb
Salvation history ends in a wedding feast.
Point 2 · Everyone invited
The king goes to the streets: all are called.
Point 3 · The wedding garment
Grace freely given must be put on and kept.
Take-home line
“Blessed are those invited to the supper of the Lamb.”
live: Accept the invitation (Matthew 22:9)
Come to a weekday Qurbana this week.
Put on the garment (Revelation 19:8)
Make a good confession before the end of the liturgical year.
2026-11-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lamb and Bridegroom, you invite us all to your wedding feast. Clothe us with your grace and make us ready for the marriage supper of the Lamb. Amen.

2026-11-12.title: Second Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: He who has the bride is the bridegroom
2026-11-12.verse: He must increase, but I must decrease.
theo: Paul feels “a divine jealousy” for the Corinthians: “I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” The apostle is like the friend who brings the bride to the bridegroom; he fears that she will be led astray to “another Jesus”.

John the Baptist says the same about himself: “He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom… rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice.” Every true minister in the Church points away from himself to Christ. Holiness is this: he must increase, I must decrease.
outline: Opening
Ask: do people meet Christ through me, or only me?
Point 1 · Betrothed to Christ
The Church is a bride kept faithful to one Lord.
Point 2 · The friend of the bridegroom
Ministers bring the bride to Christ, not to themselves.
Point 3 · He must increase
Joy in letting Christ be first.
Take-home line
“He must increase, I must decrease.”
live: Point to Christ (John 3:30)
Let someone else take the credit today.
Stay faithful (2 Corinthians 11:3)
Avoid one source of teaching that leads you from the faith.
2026-11-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, keep us faithful to you alone. Let me rejoice to hear your voice; you must increase and I must decrease. Amen.

2026-11-13.title: Second Friday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The one who comes from heaven speaks of heavenly things
2026-11-13.verse: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.
theo: Paul speaks reluctantly of being “caught up to the third heaven… into Paradise” and hearing things that cannot be told. Yet he refuses to boast except of his weaknesses. The heavenly vision does not make him proud; it makes him humble.

John's Gospel tells us why: only the one who comes from above can speak of heavenly things. “The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.” We do not climb to heaven by our own visions; heaven came down to us in the Son. To believe in him is already to have eternal life.
outline: Opening
Ask: how do we know anything about heaven?
Point 1 · Caught up to Paradise
Paul's vision leads to humility, not pride.
Point 2 · From above
Jesus comes from heaven and speaks what he has seen.
Point 3 · Believe and live
Faith in the Son is eternal life begun now.
Take-home line
“Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.”
live: Boast of weakness (2 Corinthians 12:5)
Admit one weakness honestly to God today.
Believe (John 3:36)
Make an act of faith in Jesus at midday.
2026-11-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came from above to show us the Father. Into your hands the Father has placed all things; I place my life there too. Give me the faith that is eternal life. Amen.

2026-11-14.title: Second Saturday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Let the little children come to me
2026-11-14.verse: Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them; for it is to such as these that the kingdom of heaven belongs.
theo: The Bible ends where it began, in a garden: the river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life bears fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. “They will see his face… there will be no more night.” This is the goal of the Church's journey.

And who enters? Those like children. The disciples try to keep the children away; Jesus says, “Let them come.” The Kingdom belongs to those who receive it as a gift, with open hands and trusting hearts. On this Saturday, often kept in honour of Mary, we remember her as the humble handmaid who received everything as gift.
outline: Opening
Ask: what do you most look forward to in heaven?
Point 1 · The river of life
Heaven is Eden restored: life flowing from God and the Lamb.
Point 2 · They will see his face
The deepest longing of the heart fulfilled.
Point 3 · Like children
The Kingdom is received as a gift.
Take-home line
“Let the children come to me.”
live: Bring children to Jesus (Matthew 19:14)
Pray with the children in your family tonight.
Long for his face (Revelation 22:4)
End the day with a short prayer of longing for heaven.
2026-11-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, you welcome the little ones. Make me childlike in trust, and lead me to the river of life, where I shall see your face and there will be no more night. Amen.

2026-11-16.title: Third Monday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
2026-11-16.verse: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength… You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
theo: A scribe asks which commandment is first. Jesus joins two texts of the Law, Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18: love God with everything, and love your neighbour as yourself. The scribe agrees that this is “much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices,” and Jesus tells him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”

Paul's hymn shows what this love looks like: patient, kind, not envious or boastful, not insisting on its own way. Without it, tongues, prophecy and even martyrdom are nothing. Love is not one gift among others; it is the life of the Church, the Bride's wedding garment.
outline: Opening
Ask: if love were removed from your religion, what would be left?
Point 1 · Two commandments, one love
Love of God and neighbour cannot be separated.
Point 2 · Love is patient and kind
Paul's portrait of love in practice.
Point 3 · Not far from the Kingdom
Knowing the commandment is a start; living it is the door.
Take-home line
“Without love I am nothing.”
live: Read 1 Corinthians 13 with your name
Replace “love” with your own name and examine yourself honestly.
Love in practice (Mark 12:31)
Do one patient, kind act for someone difficult today.
2026-11-16.prayer: God of love, teach me to love you with all my heart, soul, mind and strength, and my neighbour as myself. Make me patient and kind, for without love I am nothing. Amen.

2026-11-17.title: Third Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Faithful in little, faithful in much
2026-11-17.verse: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
theo: Paul calls the apostles “servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries,” and says: “it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.” Everything we have, money, time, faith, is entrusted to us; we are managers, not owners.

Jesus' parable of the dishonest manager is surprising: the master praises his shrewdness, not his dishonesty. If worldly people are clever with money for their own future, Christians should be wise in using wealth for eternity, “make friends for yourselves by means of dishonest wealth”, through generosity to the poor. And the conclusion is clear: “You cannot serve God and wealth.”
outline: Opening
Ask: if God audited your accounts today, what would he find?
Point 1 · Stewards, not owners
All is entrusted; trustworthiness is required.
Point 2 · Shrewd for eternity
Use money to make friends in heaven: give to the poor.
Point 3 · One master
You cannot serve God and wealth.
Take-home line
“Faithful in little, faithful in much.”
live: Check one small thing (Luke 16:10)
Correct one small dishonesty: a bill, a claim, a borrowed item.
Give wisely (Luke 16:9)
Set aside a fixed part of income for the poor.
2026-11-17.prayer: Lord, all I have is yours. Make me a trustworthy steward, faithful in little things, generous with the poor, and free to serve you alone. Amen.

2026-11-18.title: Third Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
2026-11-18.verse: But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
theo: Paul lists the sins that exclude from the Kingdom, then adds with tenderness: “And this is what some of you used to be. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified.” Baptism is a real change: a new identity in Christ. Christians are called to live as who they already are.

Jesus says that since John the Baptist “the good news of the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone tries to enter it by force.” The Kingdom is a gift, but it is entered with resolve: turning from sin, refusing to serve money, choosing God daily. Grace does not remove effort; it makes effort possible.
outline: Opening
Ask: what did God wash away in your baptism?
Point 1 · You were washed
Baptism gives a new identity.
Point 2 · Live who you are
Holiness is living our baptism.
Point 3 · Enter with resolve
The Kingdom is entered by decisive choices.
Take-home line
“I was washed; I will live clean.”
live: Remember your baptism
Find your baptism date and thank God for it.
One decisive choice (Luke 16:16)
Cut off one occasion of sin today.
2026-11-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you washed, sanctified and justified me in baptism. Give me the resolve to live as your child and to enter your Kingdom with all my heart. Amen.

2026-11-19.title: Third Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Bearing fruit in every good work
The seed on good soil bears fruit
2026-11-19.verse: But as for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit.
theo: Paul thanks God that the Gospel “is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world,” and prays that the Colossians may “lead lives worthy of the Lord… bearing fruit in every good work.” The Church is God's field.

Jesus explains the sower: the same seed falls on the path, rocky ground, thorns and good soil. The difference lies in the hearing. “Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.” Good soil is a heart that hears, understands and keeps the word, and so bears fruit thirty, sixty and a hundredfold.
outline: Opening
Ask: what kind of soil was your heart this week?
Point 1 · The word is bearing fruit
The Gospel grows in the whole world.
Point 2 · Four soils
Hardness, shallowness and worries choke the word.
Point 3 · Blessed ears
Hearing that understands bears fruit.
Take-home line
“Blessed are the ears that hear.”
live: Remove one thorn (Matthew 13:22)
Name one worry or distraction and give it to God.
Hear well (Matthew 13:23)
Read tomorrow's Gospel the night before.
2026-11-19.prayer: Lord, sow your word in my heart. Break up its hardness, deepen its soil, pull out the thorns, and make it bear fruit in every good work. Amen.

2026-11-20.title: Third Friday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Discipline yields the fruit of righteousness
Whoever abides in me bears much fruit
2026-11-20.verse: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
theo: Hebrews reminds suffering Christians that “the Lord disciplines those whom he loves.” Discipline “always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.” Hardship received in faith is the Father's training, not his rejection.

Jesus uses the image of the vine: the Father prunes every fruitful branch so that it bears more fruit. Pruning hurts, but its purpose is fruit. And the secret of fruitfulness is simple: abide in me. Prayer, the Word and the Qurbana keep the branch joined to the vine; “apart from me you can do nothing.”
outline: Opening
Ask: what is God pruning in your life right now?
Point 1 · Discipline from love
The Father trains the children he loves.
Point 2 · Pruned for more fruit
Pain has a purpose in God's hands.
Point 3 · Abide in me
Without Christ, nothing; with him, much fruit.
Take-home line
“Apart from him I can do nothing.”
live: Accept one pruning (John 15:2)
Offer one present difficulty to God as his pruning.
Abide (John 15:5)
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament today.
2026-11-20.prayer: Father, vinedresser of my soul, prune me with love, keep me joined to your Son, the true vine, and make me bear much fruit for your glory. Amen.

2026-11-21.title: Entrance of St Thomas the Apostle into India · Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
2026-11-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The Lord calls and sends Moses
Do not fear, I will help you
Built on the foundation of the apostles
I am the way, and the truth, and the life
2026-11-21.alt: Weekday (Third Saturday of the Dedication of the Church): 2 Timothy 4:1–8; John 17:1–8. Presentation of the Virgin Mary: Romans 8:26–30; Luke 1:46–55. Also the death anniversary of Mar Sebastian Vayalil (1986).
2026-11-21.verse: Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
theo: Today the Syro-Malabar Church remembers the arrival of the apostle Thomas in India. According to the ancient tradition of the St Thomas Christians he landed in AD 52 at Kodungallur (Maliankara, near ancient Muziris), preached the Gospel along the Malabar coast, founded Christian communities, and was martyred at Mylapore. Our Church calls him “our Father in faith”.

The readings show what an apostle is: someone called and sent. God calls Moses and sends him to Pharaoh with a promise: “I will take you as my people.” Isaiah's God says to his servant, chosen “from the ends of the earth”: “Do not fear, for I am with you.” Paul tells the Gentiles that they are “no longer strangers and aliens,” but members of God's household, “built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.” That is our story: a people at the ends of the earth, built into God's house on the foundation of Thomas.

In the Gospel it is Thomas who asks the honest question: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” And Jesus answers with one of the greatest sayings of the Gospel: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” Thomas brought to India not a philosophy but a Person, the Way himself. Later, touching the risen Lord's wounds, he would confess, “My Lord and my God!” That confession is the foundation of our faith.

Today is also the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary: the Church remembers, from ancient tradition, Mary's dedication to God from childhood. Mary and Thomas both teach us the same thing: to belong wholly to God and to follow the Way.
conn: Strangers no longer.

Ephesians 2:19 says the Gentiles are no longer strangers. For centuries the St Thomas Christians lived as a Christian people woven into Indian culture, “Christian in faith, Indian in culture, Oriental in worship”, a phrase often used of our Church.
The ends of the earth.
Isaiah 41:9 speaks of the servant taken “from the ends of the earth”. Acts 1:8 sends the apostles “to the ends of the earth”. For the Mediterranean world, India was such an end; Thomas went there.
Thomas in the Gospel.

John alone gives Thomas words: “Let us also go, that we may die with him” (11:16); “How can we know the way?” (14:5); “My Lord and my God!” (20:28). Courage, honesty, faith: the portrait of our apostle.
Margam.
The Malayalam word for the Christian faith in old Kerala usage, “Margam” (the Way), echoes John 14:6 and Acts 9:2, where Christianity is called “the Way”.
altar: The Qurbana we celebrate in the East Syriac tradition is the heritage of the St Thomas Christians, nourished for centuries through communion with the Church of the East and now celebrated in full communion with the Bishop of Rome. Every time we say “My Lord and my God” at the elevation, we repeat the faith Thomas carried to India.
outline: Opening
Ask: how did faith reach your family? Trace it back: grandparents, parish, missionaries… all the way to Thomas.
Point 1 · Called and sent
Moses and Thomas: God calls and sends with a promise.
Point 2 · No longer strangers
India received the Gospel and became part of God's household, built on the apostles.
Point 3 · The Way
Thomas asked the question; Jesus is the answer. We are the people of the Margam.
Closing image

“My Lord and my God.”

2026-11-23.title: Fourth Monday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Access to the Father through Christ
Jesus is the way, the truth and the life
2026-11-23.verse: Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me.
theo: In the last week of the year the Church hears again the promise of the Father's house: “In my Father's house there are many dwelling places… I go to prepare a place for you.” The Church on earth is the antechamber of that house.

Paul says that in Christ the dividing wall is broken down, and “through him both of us have access in one Spirit to the Father.” We are “being built together spiritually into a dwelling place for God.” Jesus is not only the destination but the Way: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
outline: Opening
Ask: what troubles your heart today?
Point 1 · Many dwelling places
The Father's house has room for us.
Point 2 · The Way
Jesus is the way to the Father.
Point 3 · Built into a dwelling
The Church is God's house being built.
Take-home line
“Do not let your hearts be troubled.”

Hand over one anxiety to Jesus each time it returns today.
Build peace (Ephesians 2:14)
Break down one wall of division in your family or parish.
2026-11-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the Way to the Father. Calm my troubled heart, build me into your dwelling, and bring me home to the place you have prepared. Amen.

2026-11-24.title: Fourth Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: A chosen race, a holy nation
2026-11-24.verse: I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also, and they will listen to my voice. So there will be one flock, one shepherd.
theo: Peter applies to the baptised the titles God gave Israel at Sinai: “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people,” called “out of darkness into his marvelous light.” Once we were “not a people”; now we are God's people.

Jesus is the gate and the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep. He has “other sheep that do not belong to this fold”; his desire is “one flock, one shepherd.” As the year ends the Church prays for her unity and for all who do not yet know the Shepherd's voice.
outline: Opening
Ask: whose voice do you follow most during the day?
Point 1 · God's own people
Baptism makes us a royal priesthood.
Point 2 · The gate and the Shepherd
Through Christ we find life in abundance.
Point 3 · One flock
Pray and work for Christian unity and mission.
Take-home line
“They will listen to my voice.”
live: Pray for unity (John 10:16)
Pray today for the unity of all Christians, especially in Kerala.
Proclaim his deeds (1 Peter 2:9)
Tell someone one thing God has done for you.
2026-11-24.prayer: Good Shepherd, you laid down your life for your sheep. Gather all your scattered children into one flock, and make us a holy people who proclaim your marvellous light. Amen.

2026-11-25.title: Fourth Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The hymn of God's plan of salvation
2026-11-25.verse: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things.
theo: Paul's great blessing opens the mystery of the whole year: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing… he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.” God's plan is “to gather up all things in him.”

Mary's Magnificat is the Church's song of that plan seen from below: God looks on the lowliness of his servant, scatters the proud, lifts up the lowly, fills the hungry. As the year ends and Annunciation approaches, the Church sings with Mary, the first of the redeemed and the image of the Church herself.
outline: Opening
Ask: what are you thankful for as this liturgical year ends?
Point 1 · Chosen before the world began
God's plan in Christ embraces us.
Point 2 · He looked on the lowly
Mary's song reverses the world's values.
Point 3 · The Church sings Mary's song
Mary is the image of the Church.
Take-home line
“The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
live: Pray the Magnificat
Pray Mary's song slowly this evening in thanksgiving for the year.
Lift up the lowly (Luke 1:52)
Do one act of respect for someone overlooked.
2026-11-25.prayer: Blessed be God, who chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. With Mary I praise you: you have done great things for me, and holy is your name. Amen.

2026-11-26.title: Fourth Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Here we have no lasting city
Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
2026-11-26.verse: Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
theo: “For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.” Hebrews reminds us that the Church is a pilgrim people; our true citizenship is in heaven. Meanwhile we offer “a sacrifice of praise to God… the fruit of lips that confess his name,” and do not neglect to do good and share.

The seventy-two return rejoicing at their success; Jesus redirects their joy: rejoice that your names are written in heaven. Then he himself rejoices in the Holy Spirit and thanks the Father for revealing these things to infants. True joy is not in what we achieve but in belonging to God.
outline: Opening
Ask: what makes you happiest: success, or belonging to God?
Point 1 · No lasting city
We are pilgrims on the way to the city to come.
Point 2 · Names written in heaven
Our deepest joy is being known and loved by God.
Point 3 · Revealed to infants
God shows himself to the humble.
Take-home line
“My name is written in heaven.”
live: Sacrifice of praise (Hebrews 13:15)
Praise God aloud for five minutes today.
Share (Hebrews 13:16)
Share a meal or gift with someone in need.
2026-11-26.prayer: Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise you because you reveal yourself to the little ones. Write my name in heaven and keep me a faithful pilgrim toward the city to come. Amen.

2026-11-27.title: Fourth Friday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: A great multitude worships before the throne
He is God not of the dead, but of the living
2026-11-27.verse: He is God not of the dead, but of the living.
theo: The Sadducees, who denied the resurrection, try to ridicule it with the story of a woman married to seven brothers. Jesus answers that they know “neither the scriptures nor the power of God.” In the resurrection life is transformed; and God is “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”

John sees the fulfilment: “a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages,” robed in white with palm branches, crying: “Salvation belongs to our God… and to the Lamb!” On the last Friday of the year we look at the end of the story: the Church gathered in praise.
outline: Opening
Ask: do you really believe in the resurrection of the body?
Point 1 · The power of God
Our hope rests on God's power, not our imagination.
Point 2 · God of the living
Those who belong to God live in him.
Point 3 · The great multitude
The Church's end is worship before the Lamb.
Take-home line
“Salvation belongs to our God and to the Lamb.”
live: Profess the resurrection
Pray the Creed slowly, pausing at “the resurrection of the body”.
Join the multitude (Revelation 7:9)
Pray today for Christians of another nation or language.
2026-11-27.prayer: God of the living, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Strengthen our faith in the resurrection and gather us with the great multitude to praise you and the Lamb for ever. Amen.

2026-11-28.title: Fourth Saturday of the Dedication of the Church · St Andrew the Apostle (anticipated)
2026-11-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Jacob's dream: the gate of heaven
Let us go with you, for God is with you
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news
2026-11-28.alt: Weekday readings: Revelation 21:22–27 (The Lord God and the Lamb are its temple); John 4:19–26 (Worship in spirit and truth). St Andrew (29 November) is kept today because 29 November is Sunday; patron's day of Archbishop Mar Andrews Thazhath. The new liturgical year begins tomorrow.
2026-11-28.verse: And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
theo: On the last day of the liturgical year the weekday readings look at the heavenly city: “I saw no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.” Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that true worshippers will worship the Father “in spirit and truth”. The whole year of feasts and Sundays has been a school for that worship.

We also keep St Andrew, the first-called. In John's Gospel he is the first to follow Jesus and immediately brings his brother: “We have found the Messiah.” Andrew is the patron of everyone who brings another to Christ. As the new year begins tomorrow with the Annunciation, Andrew reminds us that the Good News is meant to be shared: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
outline: Opening
Ask: whom did you bring closer to Christ this year?
Point 1 · The gate of heaven
Jacob discovers God in an ordinary place; the Church is the house of God.
Point 2 · Follow me
Andrew leaves his nets immediately.
Point 3 · Bring your brother
Andrew's gift: introducing others to Jesus.
Take-home line
“We have found the Messiah.”
live: Bring one person (John 1:41)
Invite someone to come with you to the Qurbana tomorrow.
Thank God for the year
Make a short review of this liturgical year in prayer.
saints: Brother of Peter, first-called, martyred, according to tradition, at Patras in Greece on an X-shaped cross.
2026-11-28.prayer: Lord Jesus, as this liturgical year ends, I thank you for all your gifts. Like Andrew, let me follow you at once and bring others to you, that we may worship the Father in spirit and truth. Amen.

2026-11-30.title: First Monday of Annunciation
2026-11-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The righteous will live by faith
2026-11-30.verse: Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father. And all were astounded at the greatness of God.
theo: Paul reminds the Galatians that “those who believe are blessed with Abraham who believed.” Christ became a curse for us “in order that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.” The Annunciation season is about this faith: Abraham's, Zechariah's, Mary's.

Coming down from the mountain, Jesus finds his disciples unable to heal a boy. “You faithless and perverse generation,” he says, and heals the child, giving him back to his father. Our failures are not the end; Christ himself acts, and all are astounded at the greatness of God.
outline: Opening
Ask: where has your faith failed recently?
Point 1 · The righteous live by faith
From Abraham to us: faith receives God's blessing.
Point 2 · Helpless disciples
Without faith and prayer we cannot overcome evil.
Point 3 · The greatness of God
Jesus heals and restores the child to his father.
Take-home line
“Lord, increase my faith.”
live: Bring a need to Jesus (Luke 9:41)
Bring one situation you cannot fix to Jesus in prayer.
Bless a child (Luke 9:42)
Pray over your children or godchildren tonight.
2026-11-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you healed the boy and gave him back to his father. Strengthen my weak faith, and let all who see your works be astounded at the greatness of God. Amen.
